liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Goin' Down The Road Feeling Bad** (3 reviews, 1 other source): The band moves into it straight out of Space, which the reviewer found especially neat; Reviewer's highlight: a fast, hard-hitting version [1][15][22][23]
- **Terrapin Station** (3 reviews): Reviewer calls the second-set Scarlet-Fire and the Terrapin awesome; Terrapin Station is described as focused and hot; the post-drums stretch is judged weaker [12][20][21]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review, 1 other source): Scarlet-Fire pairing described as smokin'; Scarlet Begonias goes into Fire On The Mountain, then returns to Scarlet Begonias [1][21]
- **Ramble On Rose** (1 review): Crowd gave the customary New York City cheer during the song in the first set [12]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer singles out the first-set Let It Grow as a smoking performance [12]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): Reviewer finds Samson and Delilah fantastic [20]
- **Hell In A Bucket** (1 review): Features sound effects that include Harley Davidson motorcycles [21]
- **Dear Mr Fantasy** (1 review): Brent's vocals shine throughout the post-drums sequence, which the reviewer finds fabulous [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd88-03-31 t01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd88-03-31 t02 Hell In A Bucket**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd88-03-31 t03 Sugaree**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd88-03-31 t04 Me & My Uncle**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd88-03-31 t05 Mexicali Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd88-03-31 t06 Brown Eyed Women**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd88-03-31 t07 When I Paint My Masterpiece**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd88-03-31 t08 Ramble On Rose**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-03-31.140737.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 23 songs; 152 min [1]
- **gd88-03-31.fm.miller.25528.sbeok.shnf**: FM broadcast; 20 songs; 137 min; rated 3.64/5 by 11 [5]. Said about its sound: Track labeling is off: Knockin' is listed where Scarlet belongs, and Scarlet actually starts after that point [17]
- **gd1988-03-31.nak300.pasternak.andrewf.90802.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 20 songs; 139 min; rated 4/5 by 7 [6]
- **gd1988-03-31.146219.sennme-80.porter.carbonetta.sirmick.flac24**: source not stated; 20 songs; 143 min [8]
- **gd88-03-31.sbd.unknown.8137.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 123 min; rated 4/5 by 24 [10]. Said about its sound: This source lets through more audience sound than an older copy the reviewer knew, which they prefer; Recording balances soundboard and crowd nicely, conveying a strong sense of the room; Reviewer finds the sound a bit hot, with too little Phil [14][19][22]

## Around the show

- Terrapin is focused with a perfect mood, but a 1977 Terrapin is harder to beat; the next night is preferred [22]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-03-31.140737.schoeps.cmc3.mk41.mattes.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Ted Mattes; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Ted Mattes' Master Audience PCM (Nakamichi DMP-100 deck, Sony ESX-HiFi/L750 tape); Schoeps CMC3/MK41 mics, ortf (1st row center, OTS) [1]
- **gd88-03-31.fm.miller.25528.sbeok.shnf**: source: Recording Info: In House FM -> Cassette Master -> Dat -> CD -> Samplitude v7.02 Professional -> SHN via Charlie Miller [5]
- **gd1988-03-31.nak300.pasternak.andrewf.90802.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Jon Pasternak; transferred by Andrew F; source: Nakamichi CM300/CP4's > patched thru one deck > Marantz PMD-420 > Maxell MX-90's w/Dolby B, set up front row of OTS. [6]. Also: Nak 300 source by Pasternak, patched with shnid 30748 in Brown Eyed Women and Ramble On Rose; Drums section patched with a short piece from the in-house FM cassette [6]
- **gd1988-03-31.146219.sennme-80.porter.carbonetta.sirmick.flac24**: taped by Steve Porter; transferred by Nick Carbonetta and SirMick; source: Source: Sennheiser ME-80s > Sony D-5 > Master Cassette - taped by Stephen Porter [8]. Also: Masters from Stephen Porter, transferred by Nick Carbonetta; tape flips patched using shnid 140737 from Ted Mattes [8]
- **gd88-03-31.sbd.unknown.8137.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [10]
